children: We hosted TBO Tek management at the Jefferies India forum. The management has reiterated confidence in delivering over 20 per cent (CC) Hotel GTV CAGR over the next five years, despite near-term West Asia disruption. Mature KAM cohorts and operating leverage should drive EBITDA growth ahead of GTV. The management noted that periods of disruption tend to increase the importance of service quality and execution, creating opportunities to deepen customer relationships. The company has remained focused on reliability and customer support through the current volatility.

The Classic acquisition is expanding TBO’s exposure to the large, resilient luxury travel segment, while AI is expected to enhance agent productivity rather than displace the travel-agent model. Currently, TBO inventory is available through Classic, but Classic’s inventory is not yet fully integrated onto TBO. It expects front-end integration by CY-end, unlocking meaningful cross-selling opportunities across both platforms.

The management estimates that wholesale contributes about 50 per cent of overall GTV, with the balance coming from retail agents. The business is largely API-led and benefits from relatively low customer churn, vs with the inherently higher churn seen in the retail-agent segment. The company has also highlighted that localisation, local-currency payments, reliability and human accountability remain key differentiators of both its API/retail offering, particularly for complex and luxury travel bookings.

title: Broker’s call: TBO Tek (Buy)
